items.ko: 반박
items.ex: Her rebuttal addressed each of his three main points.
items.exko: 그녀의 반박은 그의 세 가지 주요 논점을 하나하나 다루었다.

items.ko: 인정하다
items.ex: After seeing the new data, he had to concede the point.
items.exko: 새 자료를 본 뒤 그는 그 논점을 인정해야 했다.

items.ko: 믿을 만한
items.ex: A credible source is one that experts trust.
items.exko: 믿을 만한 출처란 전문가들이 신뢰하는 출처이다.

items.good: I would like to begin by defining the key terms.
items.ko: 저는 핵심 용어를 정의하는 것으로 시작하고 싶습니다.
bad: I would like begin by defining the key terms.
I would like to begin by define the key terms.
I would like to beginning by defining the key terms.

cz.st: I would like to begin by ___ the key terms.

items.rule: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 오고, would like 뒤에는 to부정사가 와요.

items.good: Not only does this policy cost too much, but it also fails to work.
items.ko: 이 정책은 비용이 너무 많이 들 뿐만 아니라 효과도 없습니다.
bad: Not only this policy does cost too much, but it also fails to work.
Not only does this policy costs too much, but it also fails to work.
Not only does this policy cost too much, but it also fail to work.

cz.st: Not only ___ this policy cost too much, but it also fails to work.

items.rule: Not only가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 동사가 도치되어 〈does + 주어 + 동사원형〉이 돼요.

items.good: The speaker's argument, which relies on outdated data, is unconvincing.
items.ko: 그 연설자의 주장은 오래된 자료에 의존하고 있어서 설득력이 없습니다.
bad: The speaker's argument, that relies on outdated data, is unconvincing.
The speaker's argument, what relies on outdated data, is unconvincing.
The speaker's argument, which rely on outdated data, is unconvincing.

cz.st: The speaker's argument, ___ relies on outdated data, is unconvincing.

items.rule: 쉼표 뒤에서 앞 명사를 덧붙여 설명하는 계속적 용법에는 which를 쓰고 that은 쓸 수 없어요.

items.good: If the city had banned plastic bags earlier, the river would be cleaner now.
items.ko: 그 도시가 비닐봉지를 더 일찍 금지했더라면 지금 강이 더 깨끗할 것이다.
bad: If the city would have banned plastic bags earlier, the river would be cleaner now.
If the city has banned plastic bags earlier, the river would be cleaner now.
If the city had banned plastic bags earlier, the river will be cleaner now.

cz.st: If the city ___ plastic bags earlier, the river would be cleaner now.

items.rule: 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 if절에는 had + 과거분사를 쓰고, 현재 결과는 would + 동사원형으로 말해요.

items.good: Unless we act now, the damage will become permanent.
items.ko: 지금 행동하지 않으면 그 피해는 영구적이 될 것이다.
bad: Unless we will act now, the damage will become permanent.
Unless we act now, the damage will becoming permanent.
Unless act we now, the damage will become permanent.

cz.st: Unless we ___ now, the damage will become permanent.

items.rule: 조건을 나타내는 Unless절에서는 미래의 일도 현재 시제로 쓰고 will을 붙이지 않아요.

items.good: Although the evidence is limited, the conclusion is still reasonable.
items.ko: 증거가 제한적이긴 하지만 그 결론은 여전히 합리적이다.
bad: Although the evidence is limited, but the conclusion is still reasonable.
Despite the evidence is limited, the conclusion is still reasonable.
Although of the evidence is limited, the conclusion is still reasonable.

cz.st: ___ the evidence is limited, the conclusion is still reasonable.

items.rule: although는 절을 이끄는 접속사라 뒤에 주어+동사가 오고, despite와 in spite of는 뒤에 명사(구)가 와요. although와 but은 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: My opponent has failed to address the question of cost.
items.ko: 제 상대는 비용 문제를 다루지 못했습니다.
bad: My opponent has failed addressing the question of cost.
My opponent has failed to addressing the question of cost.
My opponents has failed to address the question of cost.

cz.st: My opponent has failed ___ the question of cost.

items.rule: fail은 to부정사를 목적어로 취해요(fail to + 동사원형).

items.good: Allow me to clarify what I meant by "fair".
items.ko: 제가 "공정한"이라는 말로 의도한 바를 분명히 하겠습니다.
bad: Allow me clarify what I meant by "fair".
Allow me to clarify that I meant by "fair".
Allow to me clarify what I meant by "fair".

cz.st: Allow me ___ what I meant by "fair".

items.rule: allow + 목적어 + to부정사 형태로 써요. 또 meant by의 목적어가 빠져 있으므로 관계대명사 what이 필요해요.

items.good: She argued that the tax should be lowered.
items.ko: 그녀는 그 세금이 낮춰져야 한다고 주장했다.
bad: She argued that the tax should lowered.
She argued that the tax should been lowered.
She argued that the tax should to be lowered.

cz.st: She argued that the tax should ___ lowered.

items.rule: 조동사 should 뒤에는 동사원형이 오고, 세금은 낮춰지는 대상이므로 수동태(be + 과거분사)를 써요.

items.good: The number of students who study abroad has risen sharply.
items.ko: 해외에서 공부하는 학생의 수가 급격히 늘었다.
bad: The number of students who study abroad have risen sharply.
The number of students who studies abroad has risen sharply.
The number of student who study abroad has risen sharply.

cz.st: The number of students who study abroad ___ risen sharply.

items.rule: the number of ~는 "~의 수"라는 단수 주어라서 단수 동사(has)를 써요. a number of ~(많은 ~)는 복수 취급이에요.

items.good: The second option is far more cost-effective than the first.
items.ko: 두 번째 선택지는 첫 번째보다 훨씬 비용 효율적이다.
bad: The second option is far more cost-effective as the first.
The second option is far most cost-effective than the first.
The second option is far more cost-effectively than the first.

cz.st: The second option is far ___ cost-effective than the first.

items.rule: 두 대상을 비교할 때는 〈more + 형용사 + than〉을 쓰고, far는 비교급을 강조해요.

items.good: The proposal aims to reduce waste, save energy, and protect jobs.
items.ko: 그 제안은 쓰레기를 줄이고 에너지를 아끼고 일자리를 보호하는 것을 목표로 한다.
bad: The proposal aims to reduce waste, saving energy, and protect jobs.
The proposal aims to reduce waste, save energy, and protecting jobs.
The proposal aims to reduce waste, to save energy, and protects jobs.

cz.st: The proposal aims to reduce waste, save energy, and ___ jobs.

items.rule: 나열되는 항목은 같은 형태로 맞춰야 해요(병렬 구조). 여기서는 모두 동사원형이에요.

items.good: Rather than banning cars, the city should improve public transport.
items.ko: 차량을 금지하기보다 그 도시는 대중교통을 개선해야 한다.
bad: Rather than to banning cars, the city should improve public transport.
Instead banning cars, the city should improve public transport.
Rather than banning cars, the city should improving public transport.

cz.st: Rather than ___ cars, the city should improve public transport.

items.rule: rather than 뒤에는 앞뒤 구조를 맞춘 형태가 오는데, 여기서는 banning cars처럼 동명사(-ing)를 써요. 또 should 뒤에는 동사원형(improve)이 와요.

items.good: Critics claim that homework does more harm than good.
items.ko: 비평가들은 숙제가 득보다 실이 많다고 주장한다.
bad: Critics claims that homework does more harm than good.
Critics claim that homework do more harm than good.
Critics claim that homework does more harm as good.

cz.st: Critics claim that homework ___ more harm than good.

items.rule: homework는 셀 수 없는 단수 취급 명사라 단수 동사(does)를 써요. 비교 대상은 than으로 연결해요.

items.good: Had I known the data was flawed, I would have objected.
items.ko: 그 자료에 결함이 있다는 것을 알았더라면 나는 반대했을 것이다.
bad: Had I knew the data was flawed, I would have objected.
Had I known the data was flawed, I would objected.
Have I known the data was flawed, I would have objected.

cz.st: ___ I known the data was flawed, I would have objected.

items.rule: if를 생략하면 〈Had + 주어 + 과거분사〉로 도치되어 과거 사실의 반대를 가정해요.

items.good: Neither the moderator nor the speakers were prepared for the question.
items.ko: 사회자도 연설자들도 그 질문에 대비하지 못했다.
bad: Neither the moderator or the speakers were prepared for the question.
Neither the moderator nor the speakers were prepared to the question.
Neither the moderator nor the speakers were prepare for the question.

cz.st: Neither the moderator nor the speakers ___ prepared for the question.

items.rule: neither A nor B에서는 가까운 B(speakers)에 동사를 맞추고, 수동의 상태는 be동사 + 과거분사로 나타내요. neither는 or가 아니라 nor와 짝이에요.

items.good: The results may suggest that sleep affects memory, but more research is needed.
items.ko: 결과는 수면이 기억에 영향을 줄 수 있음을 시사하지만 더 많은 연구가 필요하다.
bad: The results may suggests that sleep affects memory, but more research is needed.
The results may suggest that sleep affects memory, but more research needs.
The results may suggest that sleep affects memory, but more research is need.

cz.st: The results may ___ that sleep affects memory, but more research is needed.

items.rule: may 같은 조동사 뒤에는 동사원형이 오고, 신중한 표현(may suggest)은 근거가 부족할 때 쓰는 완곡한 주장이에요.

items.good: As a result of the new law, accidents have decreased by ten percent.
items.ko: 새 법 덕분에 사고가 10퍼센트 줄었다.
bad: As a result the new law, accidents have decreased by ten percent.
As a result of the new law, accidents have decreased by ten percents.
As a result of the new law, accidents has decreased by ten percent.

cz.st: As a result ___ the new law, accidents have decreased by ten percent.

items.rule: as a result of ~는 "~의 결과로"라는 뜻의 덩어리 표현이에요. 뒤에 명사가 오며, accidents는 복수라 have를 써요.

items.good: Could you explain why you think the plan is unrealistic?
items.ko: 그 계획이 비현실적이라고 생각하는 이유를 설명해 주시겠어요?
bad: Could you explain why do you think the plan is unrealistic?
Could you explain why you think is the plan unrealistic?
Could you explaining why you think the plan is unrealistic?

cz.st: Could you explain why you ___ the plan is unrealistic?

items.rule: 간접의문문에서는 의문사 뒤의 어순이 〈주어 + 동사〉이므로 do를 쓰지 않아요. 주어 you에는 think를 써요.

items.good: How do you respond to the claim that the study was biased?
items.ko: 그 연구가 편향되었다는 주장에 어떻게 답하시겠습니까?
bad: How you respond to the claim that the study was biased?
How do you responding to the claim that the study was biased?
How do you respond to the claim what the study was biased?

cz.st: How do you respond to the claim ___ the study was biased?

items.rule: claim 뒤에서 내용을 설명하는 동격절은 접속사 that으로 이끌어요.

items.good: By the time the final speaker finished, the judges had already made their decision.
items.ko: 마지막 발표자가 끝났을 때 심사위원들은 이미 결정을 내린 뒤였다.
bad: By the time the final speaker finished, the judges have already made their decision.
By the time the final speaker will finish, the judges had already made their decision.
By the time the final speaker finished, the judges had already make their decision.

cz.st: By the time the final speaker finished, the judges ___ already made their decision.

items.rule: 과거의 어느 시점보다 먼저 완료된 일은 과거완료(had + 과거분사)로 나타내요.

items.good: Banning junk food advertising is one way to improve children's health.
items.ko: 정크푸드 광고를 금지하는 것은 어린이 건강을 개선하는 한 방법이다.
bad: Ban junk food advertising is one way to improve children's health.
Banning junk food advertising are one way to improve children's health.
To banning junk food advertising is one way to improve children's health.

cz.st: ___ junk food advertising is one way to improve children's health.

items.rule: 문장의 주어가 동작일 때는 동명사(-ing)를 써요. 동명사 주어는 단수 취급해서 is와 함께 써요.

items.good: Many people support the idea, yet few are willing to pay for it.
items.ko: 많은 사람이 그 생각을 지지하지만 기꺼이 돈을 내려는 사람은 드물다.
bad: Many people support the idea, yet few is willing to pay for it.
Many people support the idea, yet few are willing paying for it.
Many people support the idea, yet few are willing pay for it.

cz.st: Many people support the idea, yet few are willing ___ for it.

items.rule: be willing 뒤에는 to부정사가 오고, few는 복수 취급해요.

items.good: The speaker must have misread the graph, because the numbers do not match.
items.ko: 숫자가 맞지 않으니 연설자가 그래프를 잘못 읽었음이 틀림없다.
bad: The speaker must has misread the graph, because the numbers do not match.
The speaker must had misread the graph, because the numbers do not match.
The speaker must have misreading the graph, because the numbers do not match.

cz.st: The speaker must ___ the graph, because the numbers do not match.

items.rule: 과거 일에 대한 강한 추측은 must have + 과거분사로 표현해요.

items.good: The motion was rejected by a narrow margin.
items.ko: 그 안건은 근소한 차이로 부결되었다.
bad: The motion rejected by a narrow margin.
The motion was reject by a narrow margin.
The motion was rejecting by a narrow margin.

cz.st: The motion was ___ by a narrow margin.

items.rule: 안건은 거부당하는 대상이므로 수동태(be + 과거분사)를 써요.

items.good: The evidence on which she based her argument was weak.
items.ko: 그녀가 주장의 근거로 삼은 증거는 빈약했다.
bad: The evidence on that she based her argument was weak.
The evidence which on she based her argument was weak.
The evidence on whom she based her argument was weak.

cz.st: The evidence on ___ she based her argument was weak.

items.rule: 〈전치사 + 관계대명사〉에서는 that을 쓸 수 없고, 사물이 선행사이면 which를 써요.

items.good: The more evidence we gather, the stronger our case becomes.
items.ko: 증거를 많이 모을수록 우리의 논거는 더 탄탄해진다.
bad: The more evidence we gather, stronger our case becomes.
The more evidence we gather, the strongest our case becomes.
More evidence we gather, the stronger our case becomes.

cz.st: The more evidence we gather, the ___ our case becomes.

items.rule: 〈the + 비교급, the + 비교급〉은 "~할수록 더 …하다"라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: What worries me most is the lack of any clear evidence.
items.ko: 나를 가장 걱정시키는 것은 분명한 증거가 전혀 없다는 점이다.
bad: Which worries me most is the lack of any clear evidence.
What worries me most it is the lack of any clear evidence.
What worry me most is the lack of any clear evidence.

cz.st: ___ worries me most is the lack of any clear evidence.

items.rule: "~하는 것"이라는 뜻의 명사절은 관계대명사 what이 이끌고, 단수 주어로 취급해요.

items.good: Each of the panelists has ten minutes to present.
items.ko: 토론자 각자는 발표할 시간이 10분씩 있다.
bad: Each of the panelists have ten minutes to present.
Each of panelists has ten minutes to present.
Each of the panelist has ten minutes to present.

cz.st: Each of the panelists ___ ten minutes to present.

items.rule: each는 "각각"이라는 단수 주어라서 뒤에 복수 명사가 와도 단수 동사를 써요.

items.good: Consequently, the committee decided to postpone the vote.
items.ko: 그 결과 위원회는 표결을 미루기로 결정했다.
bad: Consequently, the committee decided postpone the vote.
Consequently, the committee decided postponing the vote.
Consequently, the committee decided to postponed the vote.

cz.st: Consequently, the committee decided ___ the vote.

items.rule: decide는 to부정사를 목적어로 취해요(decide to + 동사원형).

items.good: Scientists have been debating this question for decades.
items.ko: 과학자들은 수십 년째 이 문제를 논쟁해 오고 있다.
bad: Scientists have been debate this question for decades.
Scientists are debating this question since decades.
Scientists have debating this question for decades.

cz.st: Scientists have been ___ this question for decades.

items.rule: 과거부터 지금까지 계속되는 동작은 현재완료진행형(have been + -ing)으로 나타내요.

items.good: Instead of attacking the speaker, we should challenge the claim.
items.ko: 연설자를 공격하는 대신 우리는 그 주장에 이의를 제기해야 한다.
bad: Instead attacking the speaker, we should challenge the claim.
Instead of attack the speaker, we should challenge the claim.
Instead of attacking the speaker, we should to challenge the claim.

cz.st: Instead of attacking the speaker, we should ___ the claim.

items.rule: instead of 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 오고, should 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.

items.good: There is little evidence that the policy has worked.
items.ko: 그 정책이 효과가 있었다는 증거는 거의 없다.
bad: There is few evidence that the policy has worked.
There are little evidence that the policy has worked.
There is a few evidences that the policy has worked.

cz.st: There is ___ evidence that the policy has worked.

items.rule: evidence는 셀 수 없는 명사이므로 little을 쓰고, few·many는 셀 수 있는 복수 명사에 써요.

items.good: I strongly disagree with the previous speaker's point.
items.ko: 저는 앞선 연설자의 요점에 강하게 반대합니다.
bad: I strongly disagree the previous speaker's point.
I strongly disagree to the previous speaker's point.
I am strongly disagree with the previous speaker's point.

cz.st: I strongly disagree ___ the previous speaker's point.

items.rule: disagree는 전치사 with와 함께 써요. disagree 자체가 동사이므로 be동사를 붙이지 않아요.

items.good: While some students prefer written tests, others prefer oral exams.
items.ko: 어떤 학생들은 필기시험을 선호하는 반면 다른 학생들은 구술시험을 선호한다.
bad: While some students prefer written tests, other prefer oral exams.
While some students prefers written tests, others prefer oral exams.
While some students prefer written tests, another prefer oral exams.

cz.st: While some students prefer written tests, ___ prefer oral exams.

items.rule: some ~, others ...는 "어떤 것들은 ~, 다른 것들은 ..."이라는 뜻의 대조 표현이고, others는 복수 대명사예요.

items.q: Speaker: "You can't trust Lena's proposal on recycling; she once forgot to sort her own trash." Which fallacy is this?
o: Ad hominem
Straw man
Slippery slope
Bandwagon
items.why: 제안의 내용이 아니라 제안한 사람의 행동을 공격하므로 인신공격(ad hominem)의 오류예요.

items.q: A says, "We should spend a little more on art classes." B replies, "So you want to destroy our science programs?" B's reply is an example of which fallacy?
o: Circular reasoning
Straw man
Hasty generalization
Appeal to authority
items.why: B는 A가 하지 않은 주장을 만들어 공격하므로 허수아비 공격(straw man)의 오류예요.

items.q: "If we let students use phones for one lesson, soon they will never put them down, and school will be pointless." Which fallacy does this use?
o: False dilemma
Post hoc
Circular reasoning
Slippery slope
items.why: 작은 첫 걸음이 근거 없이 극단적인 결과로 이어진다고 주장하므로 미끄러운 경사면(slippery slope)의 오류예요.

items.q: "Either we build the new highway, or this town will disappear." What is wrong with this reasoning?
o: Straw man
False dilemma
Circular reasoning
Bandwagon
items.why: 선택지를 두 가지로만 제시하고 다른 가능성을 무시하므로 거짓 딜레마(false dilemma)예요.

items.q: "Everyone in my class is buying this app, so it must be the best one." Which fallacy is this?
o: Bandwagon appeal
Slippery slope
Appeal to authority
Hasty generalization
items.why: 많은 사람이 한다는 이유만으로 옳다고 하는 것은 편승 효과(bandwagon)의 오류예요.

items.q: "Two of my cousins failed their driving tests, so young people are terrible drivers." Which fallacy is this?
o: Argument from authority
Post hoc
Hasty generalization
Straw man
items.why: 아주 적은 사례로 전체를 단정하므로 성급한 일반화(hasty generalization)예요.

items.q: "Debate is a valuable activity because it is worth doing." Which fallacy is this?
o: Hasty generalization
Circular reasoning
False dilemma
Bandwagon
items.why: 결론과 같은 말을 이유로 되풀이하므로 순환논증(circular reasoning)이에요.

items.q: "The crime rate dropped after the new mural was painted, so the mural must have reduced crime." Which fallacy is this?
o: Appeal to authority
Circular reasoning
Post hoc
Straw man
items.why: A 다음에 B가 일어났다는 이유만으로 A가 B의 원인이라고 하는 post hoc(잘못된 인과) 오류예요.

items.q: "A famous singer says this vitamin drink improves memory, so it must work." Which fallacy is this?
o: Hasty generalization
Appeal to authority
Slippery slope
Ad hominem
items.why: 기억력에 대한 전문가가 아닌 사람의 말을 근거로 삼으므로 부적절한 권위에의 호소예요.

items.q: A student is about to finish her speech. Which sentence best signals the conclusion?
o: To sum up, we have seen two reasons.
By the way, I forgot something else.
For instance, take the case of Seoul.
On the contrary, many people disagree.
items.why: "To sum up"은 "요약하자면"이라는 뜻으로 발표의 마무리를 알리는 표현이에요.

items.q: In a formal debate, which reply disagrees most politely with the previous speaker?
o: That is completely wrong, and I think you know it very well.
I see your point, but the figures do not support it.
You clearly did not read the report before you started speaking.
Nobody sensible would ever believe a claim like that one.
items.why: 상대 의견을 인정한 뒤 근거를 들어 정중하게 반대하는 표현이에요. 나머지는 상대를 비난해요.

items.q: Which sentence is the most suitable opening line for a formal speech at a school assembly?
o: Hey guys, you ready to hear my big idea now?
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming.
Okay so, um, I guess I will just start talking now.
Right, listen up, folks, here we go then, okay?
items.why: 공식적인 자리에서는 인사와 감사로 시작하는 격식 있는 표현이 알맞아요.

items.q: Claim: "School uniforms improve discipline." Which sentence is a rebuttal to this claim?
o: Uniforms were first worn in European schools hundreds of years ago.
Schools with no uniforms report similar discipline.
Most students say that uniforms feel quite comfortable to wear.
Uniforms are available in many different colors and sizes.
items.why: 반박은 주장에 직접 맞서는 내용이어야 해요. 규율이 비슷하다는 사실은 "교복이 규율을 높인다"는 주장을 약화시켜요.

items.q: "A survey of 2,000 teenagers found that 64% sleep fewer than seven hours." What kind of evidence is this?
o: Anecdotal evidence
Statistical evidence
Expert testimony
Hypothetical example
items.why: 많은 사람을 조사해 얻은 수치이므로 통계적 근거예요.

items.q: "My neighbor lost ten kilograms on this diet, so it works." Why is this weak evidence?
o: It cites too many numbers from different sources.
It quotes a scientific study without a date.
It rests on one person's story, not a sample.
It is written in language that is too formal.
items.why: 한 사람의 경험담은 표본이 너무 작아서 일반적인 결론의 근거로 약해요.

items.q: Which thesis statement is best for a five-minute speech on school lunches?
o: School lunches are an important part of student life everywhere.
Schools should add a vegetarian dish to every menu.
Many people have strong opinions about what is served at lunch.
Lunch is the meal that most students eat in the middle of the day.
items.why: 좋은 주제문은 구체적이고 논쟁할 수 있는 입장을 담아요. 나머지는 너무 막연하거나 사실 설명일 뿐이에요.

items.q: In a claim–evidence–reasoning paragraph, what is the job of the reasoning?
o: To repeat the claim in different words
To explain why the evidence supports the claim
To list all sources in alphabetical order
To introduce a new topic for the next paragraph
items.why: 추론(reasoning)은 증거가 주장을 왜 뒷받침하는지 연결해 주는 부분이에요.

items.q: In most formal debates, which side has the burden of proof?
o: The side that speaks last
The side with more speakers
The side proposing the motion
The side that the judges happen to prefer
items.why: 주장을 내놓는 쪽(찬성 측)이 그 주장을 증명할 책임을 져요.

items.q: During cross-examination, what is the main purpose of each question?
o: To deliver a second full speech to the judges
To thank the opponent for the excellent speech
To ask the audience to vote for your team
To show the weak points in the opponent's case
items.why: 반대 심문은 질문으로 상대 주장의 약점이나 빈틈을 드러내는 단계예요.

items.q: In a formal debate, the statement that the two teams argue about, such as "This house would ban homework," is called the ___.
o: verdict
motion
rebuttal
transcript
items.why: 토론의 논제가 되는 진술을 motion이라고 해요.

items.q: Which cross-examination question is a leading question?
o: What do you personally think about this new school policy?
You agree that your data is three years old, don't you?
In which year was the study that you quoted published?
Could you please describe the main source of your data?
items.why: 유도 질문은 원하는 대답을 이미 담고 "맞죠?"라고 확인해요. 나머지는 열린 질문이에요.

items.q: Which word makes a claim more cautious, as a speaker should when the evidence is limited?
o: undoubtedly
arguably
obviously
certainly
items.why: arguably(~라고 주장할 수도 있는)는 단정을 피하는 완곡한 표현이고 나머지는 확신을 강하게 나타내요.

items.q: Cars are convenient; ___, they cause serious pollution. Which word fits best?
o: therefore
for example
however
similarly
items.why: 앞 내용과 대조되는 내용이 이어지므로 "그러나"를 뜻하는 however가 알맞아요.

items.q: Choose the best word: Cats sleep most of the day, ___ dogs usually need long walks.
o: whereas
because
unless
so that
items.why: 두 대상을 대조할 때는 "반면에"라는 뜻의 whereas를 써요.

items.q: Which opening line is a rhetorical question?
o: Last year, 3,000 students joined our school clubs.
What would you do if your phone vanished tomorrow?
An old saying tells us that practice makes perfect.
Let me begin by telling you about my trip to Busan.
items.why: 대답을 구하지 않고 청중의 관심을 끌려고 던지는 질문이 수사적 질문이에요.

items.q: A slide contains 120 words in tiny print. What is the best advice?
o: Read every word on the slide aloud to the audience.
Cut it to a few key points in larger text.
Add more words so that the slide looks complete.
Use a pale color so the text is harder to see.
items.why: 슬라이드는 핵심만 크게 보여 주고 나머지는 말로 설명하는 것이 효과적이에요.

items.q: You want to use a sentence from an online article in your presentation. What is the most responsible way?
o: Use it without comment so it sounds like your idea.
Change a few words and call it your own.
Say who wrote it and where it was published.
Skip the source because the audience cannot check it.
items.why: 정보 윤리를 지키려면 인용한 글의 저자와 출처를 밝혀야 해요.

items.q: An audience member asks a question you cannot answer. Which response is best?
o: Invent a confident answer to avoid looking weak.
Ignore the question and move to the next slide.
Tell the person that the question is not important.
Admit you are not sure and offer to find out.
items.why: 모르는 것은 솔직히 인정하고 알아보겠다고 하는 것이 신뢰를 지키는 방법이에요.

items.q: Judges are scoring a debater's argument. Which question matters most?
o: Did the speaker wear a formal jacket?
Is the claim backed by relevant evidence?
Was the speaker's voice louder than the others?
Did the speaker use the longest words?
items.why: 논증의 질은 주장이 관련 있는 근거로 뒷받침되는지에 달려 있어요.

items.q: After a presentation, which self-evaluation comment is the most useful for improving next time?
o: My talk was a complete failure from the first slide to the last.
Everything went perfectly, so I do not need to change anything.
The graph confused people, so I will explain its axes first.
I think I spoke for a little longer than I should have.
items.why: 구체적인 문제와 개선 방법이 함께 있는 성찰이 가장 도움이 돼요.

items.q: Which sentence about a new park is the most objective?
o: The park is a wonderful gift to the city's lucky families.
Only a fool would complain about the park.
The park, which opened in May, covers four hectares.
The park is clearly the best thing the council has ever done.
items.why: 객관적인 문장은 확인 가능한 사실만 담고 평가나 감정 표현을 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: In the debate, Jisoo ___ a strong point about school budgets.
o: did
took
made
gave
items.why: "주장·요점을 제기하다"는 make a point로 표현해요.

items.q: If you disagree with a proposal, you can ___ an objection.
o: stand
rise
raise
grow
items.why: "이의를 제기하다"는 raise an objection이에요. rise는 목적어를 취하지 않는 자동사예요.

items.q: From these figures, we can ___ the conclusion that prices will fall.
o: paint
draw
carve
hold
items.why: "결론을 이끌어 내다"는 draw a conclusion이에요.

items.q: In the club, Daniel often plays devil's advocate. What does he do?
o: He refuses to speak in meetings.
He always agrees with the loudest speaker.
He tells jokes to calm the room.
He argues against an idea to test it.
items.why: devil's advocate는 아이디어를 시험하려고 일부러 반대 입장에서 논쟁하는 사람이에요.

items.q: "You keep moving the goalposts!" Which situation does this complaint describe?
o: Someone arrives at the hall after the debate began.
Someone raises the required proof after it is met.
Someone refuses to give an answer to any question.
Someone repeats the same point twice in a row.
items.why: move the goalposts는 조건이 충족되자 기준을 슬그머니 바꾸는 반칙적 논증을 가리켜요.

items.q: Which statement overgeneralizes about teenagers?
o: Some teenagers spend more than five hours a day online.
Many teenagers in this survey said they sleep too little.
All teenagers are addicted to their phones.
A number of teenagers prefer reading on paper.
items.why: all처럼 예외를 허용하지 않는 말은 근거 없이 일반화한 표현이에요. 나머지는 some, many처럼 범위를 제한해요.

items.q: Which statement can be checked and proved true or false?
o: The library is the prettiest building in town.
Reading is more fun than sports.
The city library opened in 1998.
Everyone should visit the library more often.
items.why: 개관 연도는 기록으로 확인할 수 있는 사실이고 나머지는 의견이에요.

items.q: Her speech was highly ___, and half the audience changed their minds.
o: persuasion
persuasive
persuade
persuasively
items.why: be동사 뒤에서 명사 speech를 설명하려면 형용사 persuasive(설득력 있는)가 필요해요.

items.q: Which word names a statement that is assumed to be true at the start of an argument?
o: conclusion
premise
summary
rebuttal
items.why: premise(전제)는 논증을 시작할 때 참이라고 가정하는 진술이에요.

items.q: The new policy will ___ thousands of workers.
o: affect
effect
affection
effects
items.why: "~에 영향을 미치다"라는 동사는 affect예요. effect는 주로 명사(영향, 효과)로 써요.

items.q: Which sentence would be too informal for a formal debate?
o: Well, that's kinda dumb, honestly.
The proposal has several weaknesses.
I would like to challenge that statistic.
With respect, the evidence is incomplete.
items.why: kinda, dumb, honestly 같은 구어체 표현은 공식 토론에 어울리지 않아요.

items.q: In parliamentary debate, what is a "point of information"?
o: A final summary of the match read by judges
A printed list of sources given to the audience
A short break taken between two rounds
A brief question put to a speaker mid-speech
items.why: point of information은 상대가 발언하는 도중에 정중히 끼어들어 던지는 짧은 질문이에요.

items.title: Should School Uniforms Be Required?
items.text: Every autumn, our school board revisits the same question: should students wear uniforms? Supporters argue that uniforms reduce pressure to buy expensive clothes and make mornings simpler. One survey of 400 parents found that more than half spent less on clothing after uniforms were introduced. Opponents reply that clothing is a form of self-expression, and that forcing everyone to dress alike can suppress creativity. They also point out that uniforms themselves cost money, especially for families with several children. Having read both sides, I believe a compromise is wiser than a strict rule. A simple dress code, such as plain colors with no offensive slogans, would keep costs low while still allowing students to show their personality. Rather than banning choice altogether, the board should regulate only what is truly necessary.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To recommend a middle path on uniforms
To prove that uniforms harm creativity
To report a survey of local parents
To ask families to buy more clothes
qs.why: 글쓴이는 양쪽 입장을 소개한 뒤 엄격한 규칙보다 절충안(간단한 복장 규정)을 제안해요.

qs.q: According to the survey, what happened after uniforms were introduced?
o: Most parents asked the board to end the rule.
Prices in local clothing shops fell sharply.
Most students said they felt less creative in class.
More than half of parents spent less on clothes.
qs.why: 설문에서 학부모 절반 이상이 교복 도입 후 옷값을 덜 썼다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "suppress" is closest in meaning to ___.
o: copy
reward
hold back
describe in detail
qs.why: suppress creativity는 창의성을 억누른다는 뜻이므로 hold back과 가까워요.

qs.q: Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?
o: The board should remove every rule about clothing.
Uniforms are the only way to save money.
Opponents of uniforms have no valid concerns.
Some rules help, but too many are unnecessary.
qs.why: 글쓴이는 꼭 필요한 것만 규제해야 한다고 했으므로 일부 규칙은 유용하나 지나친 규칙은 불필요하다는 입장이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that uniforms themselves cost money?
o: To present a point made by the opponents
To show that the survey was not reliable
To explain why parents buy casual clothes
To argue that families should have fewer children
qs.why: 그 내용은 앞 문장의 "반대하는 사람들(They)"이 지적한 점으로 소개돼요.

items.title: A Speech Coach's Advice
items.text: Most nervous speakers make the same mistake: they try to memorize every word. When a single word slips, panic follows, and the whole talk collapses. I teach my students a different approach. First, write down only three main points and one memorable example for each. Second, practice aloud, not silently, because the mouth needs training as much as the mind. Third, record yourself once and watch the video without judging. You will notice habits, such as saying "um" or looking at the floor, that you cannot feel while speaking. Finally, remember that audiences are generally forgiving. They want you to succeed, and they rarely notice small errors. A speaker who stays calm after a stumble often appears more confident than one who never stumbles at all.

qs.q: What does the coach mainly recommend?
o: Learning a script perfectly before every talk
Preparing a few key points and practicing them
Avoiding any mistake in front of an audience
Choosing topics that the audience already knows
qs.why: 코치는 전부 외우기보다 핵심 세 가지와 예시를 준비해 소리 내어 연습하라고 해요.

qs.q: Why does the coach suggest recording yourself?
o: To send the video to the audience
To show the teacher how well you memorized
To compare your voice with a famous speaker's
To notice habits you cannot feel yourself
qs.why: 녹화하면 말하는 동안에는 느끼지 못하는 습관을 알아챌 수 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: Who does "They" refer to in "They want you to succeed"?
o: Nervous speakers
Audiences
The coach's students
Teachers
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 주어 audiences를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT advice given in the passage?
o: Prepare three main points with examples.
Practice out loud rather than silently.
Memorize each sentence of the speech.
Watch a recording of your own talk.
qs.why: 문장을 모두 외우는 것은 글에서 오히려 흔한 실수로 소개돼요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a speaker who recovers calmly from a mistake?
o: The audience may see the speaker as calm.
The speaker will certainly win the debate.
The speaker has memorized the whole speech.
The audience will remember only the error.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 실수 뒤에 침착한 연설자가 더 자신감 있어 보일 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: Bike Lanes Downtown
items.text: When the city of Millbrook added protected bike lanes to its main street last year, shop owners were divided. Some feared that removing twenty parking spaces would drive customers away. A recent study, however, tells a more complicated story. Researchers counted visitors on the street for twelve months and compared the numbers with those from the year before. Pedestrian traffic rose by eleven percent, and sales at cafes increased slightly, while two shops that depend on delivery trucks reported a small drop. The study's authors caution that one year of data is not enough to draw firm conclusions, and that other factors, such as a new festival, may have influenced the results. For now, the council plans to keep the lanes and review the evidence again next spring.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A shop owner's complaint about lost parking
A festival that brought many visitors to the street
A study with mixed but mostly positive findings
A council vote to remove the bike lanes
qs.why: 연구는 보행자와 카페 매출 증가, 일부 상점의 소폭 감소라는 엇갈린 결과를 전해요.

qs.q: What happened to pedestrian traffic during the study?
o: It rose by eleven percent.
It fell by twenty percent.
It stayed exactly the same.
It doubled in the summer.
qs.why: 보행자 수가 11퍼센트 늘었다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "firm" in "firm conclusions" is closest in meaning to ___.
o: soft
certain
expensive
early
qs.why: firm conclusions는 확실한 결론을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why do the authors mention a new festival?
o: To explain why the lanes were built downtown last year
To show another factor may have changed the numbers
To prove that cafes earn money only in spring
To suggest that the festival should be moved
qs.why: 축제 같은 다른 요인이 결과에 영향을 줬을 수 있어서 결론을 조심해야 한다는 맥락이에요.

qs.q: Which statement is true according to the passage?
o: The council has already removed all of the lanes.
All of the shops reported much higher sales.
Researchers studied the street for one week.
Two delivery-based shops lost a little business.
qs.why: 배달 트럭에 의존하는 상점 두 곳은 소폭 감소를 보고했어요.

items.title: The Debate Club's First Win
items.text: Min-ji had never spoken in front of more than five people, so when her teacher asked her to join the debate club, she almost refused. The motion for the first match was "Cities should ban cars from their centers." Her team was assigned to oppose it, which she personally found difficult. "I would rather argue for what I believe," she told her partner. He smiled and said that a good debater understands both sides. For two weeks they researched the costs to small businesses and the needs of elderly residents who cannot walk long distances. During the match, a judge asked a tough question about emergency vehicles, and Min-ji paused, took a breath, and answered calmly. They won by two points. Afterwards she admitted that arguing against her own opinion had taught her more than agreeing ever could.

qs.q: Why did Min-ji almost refuse to join the club?
o: She disliked cars and city life very much.
She was unused to speaking before crowds.
Her partner had told her it was too hard.
She had already lost a match before.
qs.why: 그녀는 다섯 명 넘는 사람 앞에서 말해 본 적이 없었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the partner mean by "a good debater understands both sides"?
o: A debater must always switch to the other team's side.
A debater should talk to both judges.
A debater needs to study views she disagrees with.
A debater should avoid strong opinions.
qs.why: 자신과 다른 입장도 이해해야 잘 논증할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the team research for two weeks?
o: How much new cars cost to buy and repair
Costs to small shops and elderly people
The long history of emergency vehicles
How judges decide the score of a match
qs.why: 소상공인의 비용과 먼 거리를 걷기 힘든 노인의 필요를 조사했어요.

qs.q: What does Min-ji's reaction to the judge's question show?
o: She could handle pressure calmly.
She did not understand the motion.
She wanted to leave the match.
She was angry with her partner.
qs.why: 그녀는 잠시 멈추고 숨을 고른 뒤 침착하게 답했어요.

qs.q: What lesson did Min-ji learn from the experience?
o: Winning matters more than learning.
Arguing against her own view can teach a lot.
Small businesses are more important than cars.
Teachers always choose the best side.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 자기 의견과 반대로 논증한 경험이 더 많은 것을 가르쳐 주었다고 말해요.

items.title: Can a Program Help You Write?
items.text: Many students now use writing assistants that suggest sentences in seconds. Proponents say these tools help beginners overcome the fear of a blank page and give instant feedback on grammar. Critics, however, worry that students may stop thinking for themselves. If a program decides how an idea should be expressed, they argue, the writer never learns to choose words carefully. Teachers also struggle to assess what a student actually understands when the final text is partly machine-made. A reasonable middle position may exist. Students could use such tools for brainstorming or checking mistakes, but write the final draft on their own and explain which suggestions they accepted. This approach is transparent, and it keeps the learning process at the center. Whether schools adopt such rules will depend on how clearly teachers can explain the purpose of each assignment.

qs.q: What does the passage mainly do?
o: It shows two views and proposes a compromise.
It proves that writing tools are harmful to students.
It explains how a writing program is built.
It tells students to stop writing drafts.
qs.why: 찬성과 비판을 소개한 뒤 절충적인 활용 방식을 제안해요.

qs.q: The word "Proponents" in the passage is closest in meaning to ___.
o: supporters
experienced teachers
complete strangers
opponents
qs.why: proponent는 어떤 생각을 지지하는 사람이에요.

qs.q: What do the critics worry about?

items.title: Reading a Chart Carefully
items.text: A graph can be accurate and still mislead. Consider a bar chart showing a company's profits for three years. If the vertical axis starts at 90 instead of zero, a rise from 92 to 96 looks enormous, even though the real increase is only about four percent. Designers sometimes do this accidentally to fit the page, but speakers who want to exaggerate their case can use the same trick deliberately. Another common problem is a missing label: without units or a source, readers cannot tell whether the numbers are millions of dollars or thousands of visitors. Before trusting any chart, therefore, ask three questions. Where does the axis begin? What exactly is being measured? And who produced the data, and why? A careful audience that asks these questions is much harder to persuade with a flashy picture.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Bar charts are always better than other kinds of graphs.
Charts need checking before they are trusted.
Companies should publish their profits.
Designers must always start axes at ninety.
qs.why: 글은 그래프가 정확해도 오해를 부를 수 있으니 세 가지 질문으로 확인하라고 말해요.

qs.q: In the example, about how large is the real increase from 92 to 96?
o: About four percent

About ninety-six percent
qs.why: 92에서 96으로는 약 4퍼센트 올랐어요.

o: slowly

items.title: A Letter About the Garden
items.text: Dear Editor, I am writing in response to the proposal to replace the community garden on Elm Street with a parking lot. Supporters of the plan say that the neighborhood lacks parking and that the lot would bring more shoppers. I understand this concern, but I question whether the benefit is as large as claimed. The garden currently feeds about thirty families, hosts a weekly children's workshop, and, in summer, provides the only shade on the block. Moreover, there are two underused lots only three streets away that could hold the same number of cars. Before the council votes, I urge it to study these alternatives. A decision that cannot be undone deserves more careful thought than a single meeting allows. Yours sincerely, Hana Park

qs.q: What is the writer's purpose?
o: To ask the council to try other options
To thank the council for its helpful plan
To announce a new children's workshop
To advertise shops on Elm Street
qs.why: 글쓴이는 표결 전에 대안을 검토해 달라고 촉구해요.

items.title: Why Teenagers Sleep Less
items.text: Teenagers around the world sleep less than experts recommend, and a recent review of forty studies suggests several causes. Biological changes during puberty shift the body clock later, so many teenagers feel alert at midnight but exhausted at seven. Early school start times make the problem worse. In one trial, schools that began an hour later reported that students attended class more regularly and fell asleep less often during lessons. Screen use before bed also plays a role, although the evidence is weaker than many headlines imply. The authors stress that these findings show association rather than proof of cause, and that families differ widely. Even so, they conclude that adjusting school schedules is a low-cost step worth testing in more districts.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why teenagers should avoid all screens
Several likely causes of teenagers' short sleep
A new alarm clock designed for students
How to teach lessons late in the evening
qs.why: 글은 사춘기의 신체 변화, 이른 등교 시간, 화면 사용 등 여러 원인을 설명해요.

qs.why: 시작 시간을 늦춘 학교에서 학생 출석이 더 규칙적이었고 수업 중 졸음이 줄었어요.

qs.why: 연관성은 함께 나타난다는 뜻일 뿐 한쪽이 원인이라는 증명은 아니라는 뜻이에요.

o: completely forget that
